projects.name: Analytics Dashboard
projects.description:
An analytics dashboard platform that ingests and processes customer CSV files, analyzes application log data, and presents insights through visualization components. Scope covers data ingestion pipelines, log analysis, a serving/API layer, and a frontend visualization layer.

Tags: analytics, dashboard, data-pipeline, visualization, logs

tasks.name: Milestone 1: Foundations & Data Contracts
tasks.details: Establish the technical baseline before any pipeline work: repository/tooling setup, schema definitions for customer CSV data and application log events, and shared conventions for identifiers, timestamps, and environment configuration. Output: an agreed schema spec plus a runnable local dev environment.

tasks.name: Milestone 2: Customer CSV Ingestion & Processing
tasks.details: Build the pipeline that lands customer CSV files, validates and cleans them, and produces analytics-ready customer datasets. Includes file arrival handling, schema validation, deduplication, normalization, and aggregation into customer metrics.

tasks.name: Milestone 3: Application Log Ingestion & Analysis
tasks.details: Build the log pipeline: parse application log formats, extract structured fields, derive error/performance metrics, and compute time-bucketed aggregates. Includes parsing strategy, anomaly/error-rate derivation, and log retention/rollup policy.

tasks.name: Milestone 4: Data Storage & Serving API
tasks.details: Persist processed datasets in an analytics store and expose them through a query API for the dashboard. Includes storage design, metric query endpoints, filtering/time-range support, caching, and access control.

tasks.name: Milestone 5: Visualization Components & Dashboard UI
tasks.details: Deliver the user-facing dashboard: reusable chart components, dashboard layout, filters/date-range controls, and wiring to the serving API. Covers component library, customer analytics views, and log/health views.

tasks.name: Milestone 6: Quality, Observability & Release Readiness
tasks.details: Assure the dashboard is reliable before launch: automated test coverage across pipelines and UI, data quality checks, monitoring/alerting for pipeline failures, documentation, and a staged rollout plan.

tasks.name: Set up repo, tooling and local dev environment
tasks.details: Create the repository skeleton (pipeline service, serving API, dashboard app), configure linting/formatting, package manager, env var template, and a one-command local dev startup with containerized dependencies (DB + queue). Acceptance: a new developer can clone and run the stack locally from the README.

tasks.name: Write customer CSV schema spec and sample fixtures
tasks.details: Document every expected customer CSV column with type, nullability, allowed values, and example rows. Produce 3-5 anonymized sample CSV fixtures (clean, messy, malformed) that all later validation work can be tested against. Acceptance: schema doc reviewed and fixtures committed.

tasks.name: Write application log event schema spec and sample log lines
tasks.details: Define the structured log event model (timestamp, level, service, request id, latency, status, message) and document all log formats emitted by the application. Include a fixture set of representative raw log lines covering each format and severity. Acceptance: schema doc plus fixtures committed.

tasks.name: Define shared conventions: IDs, timestamps, timezone and env config
tasks.details: Agree on canonical ID formats, UTC storage with per-user display timezone, date-range semantics for analytics windows, naming conventions for metrics, and environment configuration keys. Acceptance: one-page conventions doc referenced by schema specs.

tasks.name: Build customer CSV ingestion entry point
tasks.details: Add the entry point for customer CSV arrival: a secure upload endpoint plus a watched folder/S3-style drop, with file registration (source, size, checksum, received_at) and enqueueing of a processing job. No parsing logic here. Acceptance: uploading a CSV creates a registered file record and one queued job, covered by an integration test.

tasks.name: Implement CSV parsing and schema validation with reject report
tasks.details: Stream-parse CSV files (handle quoting, encoding, delimiters, large files), validate every row against the agreed schema, and route invalid rows to a reject/quarantine table with row-level error reasons. Emit counts for accepted vs rejected rows. Acceptance: the clean/messy/malformed fixtures produce the expected accept/reject counts.

tasks.name: Implement customer data cleaning and normalization
tasks.details: Normalize accepted rows: type coercion, trimming, null handling, country/currency code standardization, and deduplication on the canonical customer key (keep latest by updated_at). Write results to the staging customer table with a processing run id. Acceptance: messy fixture produces deduplicated, normalized output validated by unit tests.

tasks.name: Compute customer metric aggregates
tasks.details: Aggregate cleaned customer data into the dashboard metrics: total/new/active customers, segment and plan breakdowns, churn and retention cohorts, and revenue/ARPU style rollups where data allows. Define each metric formula explicitly. Acceptance: metric definitions documented and results verified against a manually computed fixture.

tasks.name: Make customer pipeline idempotent and re-runnable
tasks.details: Ensure re-processing the same file does not double-count: use checksums and run ids, delete-and-replace per source file, and support a backfill command for historical files. Acceptance: running the same file twice yields identical aggregates; backfill over 3 months of fixtures reproduces expected totals.

tasks.name: Set up application log collection and shipping
tasks.details: Collect application logs into the analytics landing zone: tail/rotate local log files or subscribe to the existing log sink, batch and gzip on ship, track offsets so no lines are lost or duplicated. Acceptance: a test log file grows to 10k lines and all lines arrive exactly once.

tasks.name: Implement log parser for each application log format
tasks.details: Write a parser per documented log format (plain text, JSON lines, multi-line stack traces) that extracts timestamp, level, service, request id, status, latency, and message. Count and quarantine unparseable lines with reasons. Acceptance: every fixture line parses to expected fields or is quarantined with a reason.

tasks.name: Normalize and enrich structured log records
tasks.details: Map parsed records to the canonical log event model: UTC timestamps, level enum, service name normalization, error fingerprinting (grouping messages into error classes), and request-level correlation by request id. Acceptance: enriched records pass schema validation and error fingerprints group a known sample correctly.

tasks.name: Derive error-rate, latency and volume metrics from logs
tasks.details: Compute log-derived metrics per service: error/warn rates, p50/p95/p99 latency, request volume, and top error fingerprints. Each formula documented and validated against a hand-computed fixture. Acceptance: metrics match expected values within defined tolerance.

tasks.name: Build time-bucket rollups and log retention policy
tasks.details: Pre-aggregate log metrics into hourly and daily buckets for fast dashboard queries, and implement retention: keep raw logs 30 days, rollups indefinitely (configurable). Acceptance: rollups backfill from fixtures for 30 days and raw-log cleanup job verified in a dry run.

tasks.name: Design analytics store schema and partitioning
tasks.details: Choose the analytics store and model tables for customer metrics, log metrics, and rollups: column types, primary keys, time partitioning/clustering, and indexes for the dashboard's known query patterns. Acceptance: DDL committed with a written rationale and a sample query performing well on seeded data.

tasks.name: Implement metrics write path into the analytics store
tasks.details: Load computed customer and log metrics from the pipelines into the analytics store with upserts keyed by metric + dimension + time bucket. Handle partial failures with retry and emit load success/failure events. Acceptance: concurrent loads are idempotent and a mid-load failure leaves no duplicate rows.

tasks.name: Implement metric query API endpoints
tasks.details: Expose REST endpoints for each dashboard need: KPI summary, customer series with dimension breakdown, log health series, and top error fingerprints. Consistent response envelope, documented OpenAPI schema. Acceptance: endpoint contract tests pass against seeded data.

tasks.name: Implement filters, time ranges and pagination semantics
tasks.details: Support date-range presets and custom ranges, dimension filters (plan, segment, service, level), bucket granularity selection with automatic rollup fallback, and cursor pagination for list endpoints. Acceptance: edge cases (DST boundary, empty range, unknown filter) return documented, tested behaviour.

tasks.name: Add response caching and performance budgets
tasks.details: Cache query responses keyed by endpoint + normalized filter params with short TTLs and invalidation on new data loads. Establish budgets (p95 under 400ms for dashboard endpoints on 1M rows) and add a benchmark test. Acceptance: cache hit rate and latency measured in a load test.

tasks.name: Add API authentication and access control
tasks.details: Protect read endpoints with token/session auth, enforce role-based visibility (e.g. customer PII aggregates restricted), rate limit per client, and never return raw customer rows from aggregate endpoints. Acceptance: unauthorized and over-privileged requests rejected in tests.

tasks.name: Set up dashboard app shell, routing and design tokens
tasks.details: Create the frontend app with routing between Customer Analytics and Log Health pages, a persistent top bar/sidebar, theme tokens (colors for metrics, chart palette), and error boundary. Acceptance: navigation works with mocked data, no console errors, tokens documented.

tasks.name: Build reusable chart component library
tasks.details: Create a small set of typed, reusable chart components: KPI tile with delta, time-series line/area, stacked bar, donut, and top-N table with inline bars. Each handles loading, empty and error states plus accessible text summaries. Acceptance: a component gallery page renders every variant with fixture data and unit snapshots.

tasks.name: Implement global filter bar with date-range and URL state
tasks.details: Build the shared filter bar: date-range presets and custom picker, dimension filters (plan, segment, service), and granularity selector. Filter state lives in the URL so views are shareable and refresh-safe. Acceptance: changing filters updates the URL and refetches data without full page reload.

tasks.name: Build API data-fetching layer with loading and error states
tasks.details: Create a typed API client and query hooks for each endpoint: request de-duplication, retries, cancellation on filter change, and a consistent loading/skeleton/error/retry UI pattern. Acceptance: simulated 500s and slow responses show friendly error and retry states without layout shift.

tasks.name: Build customer analytics dashboard view
tasks.details: Compose the Customer Analytics page: KPI tiles (total/new/active/churned), customer growth trend, segment and plan breakdowns, retention cohort view. Wire to the customer endpoints and the global filters. Acceptance: matches approved mock for the default 30-day view and handles zero-data gracefully.

tasks.name: Build application log health dashboard view
tasks.details: Compose the Log Health page: error-rate trend per service, latency percentiles (p50/p95/p99), request volume, and top error fingerprints table with drill-down to counts by time bucket. Acceptance: matches approved mock and clearly distinguishes no-data from zero-traffic states.

tasks.name: Responsive layout, accessibility and empty-state polish
tasks.details: Make both pages usable from 1280px down to tablet width, add keyboard navigation, color-blind-safe chart palettes, chart alt summaries, focus states, and purposeful empty states. Acceptance: automated a11y audit passes and a manual responsive check covers three breakpoints.

tasks.name: Write pipeline test suite (unit + integration)
tasks.details: Cover CSV parsing/validation/cleaning/aggregation and log parsing/enrichment/metrics with unit tests plus end-to-end integration tests using the fixture datasets. Set a coverage target for pipeline modules and run in CI. Acceptance: suite green in CI, coverage target met.

tasks.name: Add dashboard component tests and e2e smoke path
tasks.details: Unit/snapshot tests for chart components and filter state, plus one Playwright-style e2e smoke test that loads the dashboard, changes the date range, and asserts KPIs and charts render with API mocks then real seeded data. Acceptance: e2e smoke passes in CI.

tasks.name: Implement data quality checks and freshness alerts
tasks.details: Add scheduled checks: expected row volumes, null/duplicate rate thresholds, schema drift detection, and data freshness SLAs per pipeline. Emit a quality report and alert on breach. Acceptance: deliberately broken fixture triggers the correct alerts in a staging run.

tasks.name: Add pipeline observability: run metrics, logs and failure alerts
tasks.details: Instrument each pipeline stage with structured logs, duration/throughput/error metrics, and a dead-letter queue for failed jobs. Configure alerts for repeated failures and stuck jobs. Acceptance: a forced job failure produces a metric, a log entry, and an alert notification in staging.

tasks.name: Write operator docs, metric definitions and runbook
tasks.details: Produce user-facing docs: what each dashboard metric means and how it is computed, how to upload a CSV, how to backfill, and a runbook for common failures (bad schema, stuck job, stale data). Acceptance: a teammate unfamiliar with the system can follow the runbook to recover a failed pipeline.

tasks.name: Define staged rollout plan and launch checklist
tasks.details: Plan internal pilot (1-2 teams) then wider release: feature flags, feedback capture, success criteria (usage, freshness, latency), and a rollback/kill-switch procedure. Acceptance: checklist signed off with owners and dates.
